decision: Is our team ready to publish AI-drafted marketing work, and does each citation in a draft meet the rules before it ships?
limitations: It is a rule check, not a fact checker. A citeable verdict means the citation has the right parts; it cannot tell whether the study exists. It does not replace legal or compliance review.
The draft sweep only spots figures written with %, "percent", "x" or $. Plain counts such as "110 startups" go unflagged, so read the draft for every number.
Readiness credits tools only against the engine's six task labels, matched exactly, and scores what you say was verified. It cannot see your plan's real training setting.
Input it doesn't recognise produces no output rather than an error; check the result reflects your numbers.
review: The named reviewer opens every cited document before publish, and the policy owner checks the training-on-inputs setting on the plan itself. Legal or compliance reviews disclosure, data and claims rules for your markets.
